ministry_ne: कानून, न्याय तथा संसदीय मामिला मन्त्रालय
summary:
The Nepal Law Commission (First Amendment) Bill, 2083 has been prepared to amend the Nepal Law Commission Act, 2063 (Objectives and Reasons). The main purpose of this bill is to modify the structure and scope of work of the Nepal Law Commission to develop it as a center of excellence in the field of law drafting and legal and judicial research, and to make the operations carried out by the Commission prompt, effective, and high quality (Objectives and Reasons). When this bill comes into force is not stated in the bill (not stated in the bill).

If the relevant ministry of the Government of Nepal needs to draft a bill based on detailed study and research, it must have the draft of such bill prepared through the Commission (Explanatory Note, Page 4). The Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs may request the Commission to draft model laws that the Government of Nepal needs to make for provincial and local levels (Three-Column Statement, Section 14, Section 21b, Subsection 1, Page 12). Provincial and local levels may request the Commission to draft necessary bills for them (Three-Column Statement, Section 14, Section 21a, Subsection 1, Page 12).

This bill modifies the formation and structure of the Nepal Law Commission (Explanatory Note, Page 1). The Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs serves as the Chairperson of the Commission (Three-Column Statement, Section 2, Section 4, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 1). There is one Vice-Chairperson appointed by the Government of Nepal from among persons who have worked in a special category post in the field of law drafting or have achieved at least 20 years of work experience in the field of law drafting (Three-Column Statement, Section 2, Section 4, Subsection 1, Clause b, Page 1). There are two members appointed by the Government of Nepal from among persons who have achieved at least 15 years of work experience in the field of law drafting (Three-Column Statement, Section 2, Section 4, Subsection 1, Clause c, Page 2). There is one member appointed by the Government of Nepal from among persons who have achieved at least 15 years of experience in teaching or research work in the constitutional or legal field (Three-Column Statement, Section 2, Section 4, Subsection 1, Clause d, Page 2). The Secretary of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs serves as an ex-officio member and the Secretary of the Commission serves as the ex-officio member-secretary (Three-Column Statement, Section 2, Section 4, Subsection 1, Clauses e and f, Page 2). At least one among the appointed members must be a woman (Three-Column Statement, Section 2, Section 4, Subsection 2, Page 2). To be eligible as Vice-Chairperson and member of the Commission, a person must be a Nepali citizen, have completed 45 years of age, hold at least a master's degree in law from a university recognized by the Government of Nepal, not be a member of any political party at the time of appointment, and not have been convicted by a court of corruption, money laundering, human trafficking, drug sales or trafficking, passport misuse, rape, or a criminal offense showing moral turpitude (Three-Column Statement, Section 3, Section 6, Page 3). The term of office for the Vice-Chairperson and appointed members is 5 years (Three-Column Statement, Section 4, Section 7, Subsection 1, Page 4). The Vice-Chairperson and appointed members are full-time officials of the Commission, and the Vice-Chairperson receives remuneration and facilities equal to the head of a constitutional body while members receive remuneration and facilities equal to a member of a constitutional body (Three-Column Statement, Section 10, Section 14, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 9). The Vice-Chairperson carries out responsibilities including presiding over Commission meetings in the absence of the Chairperson, performing and causing to be performed functions carried out by the Commission, coordinating and cooperating with law commissions of other countries, and taking initiative in making quality laws (Three-Column Statement, Section 9, Section 13, Subsection 1, Pages 8-9). The Secretary of the Commission acts as the administrative chief of the Commission and prepares and submits proposals for Commission meetings (Three-Column Statement, Section 11, Section 15, Subsection 2, Clause d1, Page 10). The main functions and duties of the Commission include evaluating the implementation status of existing Acts and sending reports to the relevant ministry, operating and managing the Nepal Law Information System, studying and reviewing laws enacted by provincial or local levels, conducting study and research regarding reforms needed in the field of criminal and civil law, studying whether Nepal should become a party to any international treaty and making recommendations, and making a law drafting manual (Three-Column Statement, Section 6, Section 10, Pages 4-5). The Commission must draft and send a bill requested by provincial or local levels generally within 90 days of request (Three-Column Statement, Section 14, Section 21a, Subsection 2, Page 12). The Commission must prepare and submit the draft of a model law requested by the Ministry within 90 days to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Three-Column Statement, Section 14, Section 21b, Subsection 2, Pages 12-13). A separate fund for the Commission is not stated in the bill (not stated in the bill), but additional financial expenses will be managed from the allocated budget (Financial Note).

Sections 5, 9, 12, and 19 of the principal Act are repealed (Section 20, Three-Column Statement, Section 18, Section 20, Page 15). What happens to the staff, assets, and funds of the repealed provisions or bodies is not stated in the bill (not stated in the bill).
title: Nepal Law Commission (First Amendment) Bill, 2083
